newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks capture cautious gains at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks capture cautious gains at open.

text.p: The Australian share market trailed record breaking U.S. markets higher at the open on Tuesday although enthusiasm was restrained ahead of the federal government's 1997/98 budget to be released later in the day.
The All Ordinaries index added nine points to 2,533.8.

While Wall Street provided some impetus, traders said early enthusiasm was likely to be tempered in the afternoon as the market waited to evaluate the government's fiscal programme, which was due to be announced after trading hours.
"A few things have been leaked on the Budget but realistically people are going to wait and see what impact it does actually have," said dealer Peter Struk of brokerage Reynolds and Co.
"Initially you will have the market up on the back of Wall Street but it will taper off towards the end of the day."
Building materials, aluminium and sugar group CSR lost ground, down 7.3 cents to A$4.69 (US$3.66) following news on Monday of a slump in full-year profits amid depressed housing sector conditions.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to one, while about 38 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
